Archive study · Possession ≠ complete ownership

Who Owns the Archive?

A fashion archive is not one asset. It is a governed constellation of physical objects, copyrights, marks, contracts, files, testimony, privacy interests, access permissions, and institutional obligations.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

“Who owns the archive?” sounds singular because the boxes share a room. Under U.S. copyright law, however, ownership of a material object is distinct from ownership of copyright embodied in it. A garment, sketch, photograph, interview recording, database export, and trademark file can therefore sit together while their control travels through different records.

The first institutional task is not to crown one owner. It is to make an item-and-rights map that distinguishes custody, title, copyright, license, confidentiality, access, conservation duty, digitization permission, and interpretive authority—then sends disputed or jurisdiction-specific conclusions to counsel.

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · INVENTORY

What is actually here?

Assign a persistent identifier to each object, file, recording, agreement, credential, and related record. Preserve original order and provenance before reorganizing for convenience.

PROPOSALS08S65

02 · SEPARATE

Which interest attaches to which item?

Record physical title, copyright authorship and transfers, trademark or design records, contract limits, privacy, access, and conservation separately. One accession row may need several rights rows.

VERIFIEDS63

03 · GOVERN

Who may possess, use, reproduce, lend, digitize, describe, and dispose?

Turn vague control into verbs, responsible parties, territory, term, approval, exceptions, recovery, and a source document. Unknown is a valid status; guessed ownership is not.

PROPOSALS63S64

04 · STEWARD

What must remain usable after a transfer?

Require identifiers, checksums, condition notes, formats, contextual narration, rights evidence, audit history, and a correction route to travel with the archive.

PROPOSALS08S66

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Fragmenting the archive into rights can obscure its cultural wholeness; treating it as culturally whole can obscure the rights and labor of photographers, makers, sitters, donors, employees, and communities. Ethical stewardship must keep both views in frame.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Select ten representative archive items and give each a stable identifier.
  2. For each, separate custody, material title, copyright, contract, privacy, access, and conservation evidence.
  3. Name the canonical record supporting each asserted power and mark every unknown.
  4. Send disputed title, copyright, contract, probate, privacy, and foreign-law questions to qualified counsel.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical 3,500-word essay
  • Twelve-minute object-and-rights film
  • Ten-frame “one room, many rights” carousel
  • Four archive-ownership verticals
  • Archive Rights Constellation interactive
  • Newsletter, registrar, founder, and counsel-prep editions

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Open the archive door and refuse the singular noun. Follow one Worth dress through object title, house attribution, designer credit, donor history, accession, image status, and museum custody. Then build the rights constellation without pretending the object record answers private contracts or title disputes.

02

SHORT 01 — “Owning the garment is not automatically owning every photograph, sketch, story, or copyright around it.” Show six separate evidence lanes.

03

SHORT 02 — “The archive is a room. Ownership is a map.” Every asserted verb—hold, copy, lend, publish, sell, destroy—must point to a record.

04

CAROUSEL — WHO OWNS THE ARCHIVE? / WHICH ITEM? / PHYSICAL TITLE / COPYRIGHT / CONTRACT / PRIVACY / ACCESS / CONSERVATION / INTERPRETATION / COUNSEL GATE.

05

NEWSLETTER — Subject: The archive does not have one owner just because it has one address. Walk readers through the ten-item audit and the difference between custody and underlying rights.

06

REGISTRAR EDITION — A field-by-field transfer checklist for identifier, origin, condition, rights evidence, restrictions, files, checksums, context, and correction history.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
